text:
alex: Customer support escalated ticket INC-4321. They've seen p99 on /v1/chat/generate jump from ~300ms to ~4-6s since this morning's runtime deploy. Reports correlate with a big rise in kv/prefix cache misses on the serving shard. Raising to eng-runtime for triage.

maya: Thanks — can you attach the support logs + a small repro request? Do we have shard ids and prometheus spans?

alex: Pasted logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T12:28:03Z shard=shard-12 req_id=abc123 prefix_key=hdr:client:session:abcd miss=true
2026-03-15T12:28:03Z shard=shard-12 req_id=abc124 prefix_key=hdr:client:session:abcd-1 miss=true
2026-03-15T12:28:04Z shard=shard-12 req_id=abc125 latency_ms=4200
```
Prom query I ran: `sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) by (shard) / sum(rate(kv_requests_total[5m])) by (shard)` shows miss rate on shard-12 jumped 2% -> 36% at 12:25 UTC.

rachel: That time aligns with deploy 9f4c2b8. That change touched header normalization where we started including X-Client-* headers in the cache key (to preserve per-client routing). If those headers have high cardinality or vary order/case, that'll explode key space.

sam: Repro idea: send same request with header permutations and observe different prefix_key printed. Quick curl to test:
```
# A (works)
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -H "X-Client-ID: app-1" -d '{"input":"hi"}'
# B (same client different header order -> new cache key)
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/generate -H "X-Client-ID: app-1" -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
Both produce identical responses but code-path produced different prefix_key values in logs. That suggests cache key construction depends on header ordering or casing.

maya: Yep — I pulled the normalization helper, it concatenates headers in iteration order and doesn't sort or lowercase keys. Patch idea: canonicalize headers (lowercase), whitelist only stable headers (Authorization, Accept-Language, Red-Region, X-Red-Client) and sort before hashing. Also add a stable hash function with a prefix namespace.

rachel: For immediate mitigation we can: 1) rollback 9f4c2b8 on runtime routing config (fast, canary rollback), 2) temporarily increase prefix cache TTL from 60s -> 300s on affected shards to reduce cold misses, 3) enable warmup drip jobs to prepopulate top prefixes, 4) add emergency circuit to route heavy clients to dedicated pool. Which do we want to do now?

alex: Support wants asap. I'd start with TTL bump + enabling warmup on shard-12 cluster and initiate revert of the header change in canary. Sam can you run the TTL change?

sam: On it. Command I used to update shard config: `rbctl config apply --cluster shard-12 --set prefix_cache.ttl=300` — applied at 12:40 UTC. Also started a warmup job for top-20 prefixes.

opsbot: Deploy bot: Revert request queued for deploy-pipeline (req #DEP-887). Can trigger hotfix deploy to canary in ~6 minutes.

maya: I'll prepare the normalization patch and tests. Patch will: lowercase header names, filter to whitelist, sort keys, then compute sha256 of canonical string. Minimal diff so we can hotfix quickly. Also adding unit test for header permutations.

rachel: Also creating an alert: `kv_cache_key_entropy` > 5.0 triggers paging. We didn't have entropy visibility before — let's add dashboard panel and an on-call rule.

alex: Repro steps for support (condensed): 1) run two identical requests changing header order, 2) check logs for prefix_key differences, 3) collect `kv_cache_miss_total` for impacted shard. Attach their request ids to the ticket.

sam: Patch applied to canary (hotfix 9f4c2b8-revert + header-canonicalize). Canary metrics look promising: miss rate on canary nodes dropped from 34% -> 3% in 3m and p99 latency down to ~380ms. Rolling this out to shard-12 now.

alex: Good work. Follow-ups: - maya to land canonicalization + tests + small migration doc - rachel to add entropy alert + dashboard - ops to run a sweep to warm top prefixes across clusters - support to confirm with customer that p99 regressed back to baseline.

maya: I'll open PR and include a short blurb in the changelog about header whitelist behavior.

rachel: Noting root cause: accidental high-cardinality headers included in cache key + non-deterministic header ordering. Permanent fix is canonicalization + whitelist + better telemetry for cache key entropy.

alex: Closing on our side once support confirms. :white_check_mark:
